solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mobile phone's extremely expensive Nokia, constraining Rex to not lose it

indicators.note: constraining means holding within, so the rearranged letters close round the king's letter
mobile means able to move about, so these letters are free to shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of expensive

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a pricey Nokia handset is keeping the king from staying cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like part of 'Mobile phone' but is the anagram signal; 'extremely' takes the ends of 'expensive', and 'constraining' puts the king inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for staying calm: to not lose it is to remain composed rather than fly into a temper.

clue.text: Good to occupy awfully nice room designed for efficiency

indicators.note: to occupy means to sit inside, so the letter for good goes within the other letters
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of nice room are jumbled

explanation.surface: An awful but nice room has been designed with efficiency in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges NICE ROOM, and 'to occupy' places G within that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design arranges workplaces and tools so people can use them efficiently and comfortably.

clue.text: Stroke kitty, changing sides

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so the R for right is swapped for L for left

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, a purse

explanation.surface: Someone strokes a kitten, then moves round to the other side of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitty' is a cat in the surface but a fund of money in the wordplay; 'changing sides' turns its R (right) into L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A single beat of the heart or throb at the wrist can be called a stroke, as in a regular pulsation.

clue.text: Close mate upset about right nasty experience

parts.note: close in the sense of near, nigh

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the letter for right
upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of mate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A close friend is upset about some nasty thing that happened, right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of 'mate' to TMAE, and 'about' wraps that round the R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream, or by extension any frightening or very unpleasant episode, is a nightmare.

clue.text: Special oriental sponge produces natural lubricant

parts.note: E for East, the oriental direction
to sponge is to scrounge, which in slang is to bum

explanation.surface: A special sponge from the East produces its own natural oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' is a noun in the surface but a verb, to cadge, in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The oily secretion of the skin's glands keeps hair and skin supple, acting as the body's own lubricant.

clue.text: Arabic fellow elected leader of Arabic country

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a gent
someone elected is in office, IN

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of the second Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arab man has been elected to lead an Arab nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabic country' looks like it wants a Middle Eastern state, but 'Arabic' only feeds the wordplay and the country is South American.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Educated woman eats a dish from India

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the a goes inside the name

parts.note: Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita, so she is the woman being educated

explanation.surface: A well-educated woman tucks into an Indian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a working-class woman going to university; so the educated woman is RITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or other vegetables and spices.

clue.text: Manuel's the dope up before court for lack of care

indicators.note: before means the reversed letters come ahead of the court abbreviation
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so these letters go backwards

parts.note: Manuel is the Spanish waiter in Fawlty Towers, and the Spanish for the is el
dope means information, gen

explanation.surface: Fawlty Towers' Manuel shows such carelessness that he ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel is the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, so his 'the' is Spanish; 'up' turns the first two pieces to NEGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect means failing to give proper attention, which is a lack of care.

clue.text: More than one tea dance

indicators.note: more than one tea is taken as two of them, so the word for tea is doubled

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Several cups of tea served at a tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea dance' looks like one phrase, but 'tea' feeds the wordplay and 'dance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Incline to embrace German philosopher

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold around, so the letter for German goes inside

parts.note: a ship heels when it leans over, so to incline is to heel

explanation.surface: Someone leans in to hug a German thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was a German idealist thinker, so he is an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Be unwanted and become mendicant?

definitions.meaning: said of something nobody takes up, like a job or offer left unclaimed
a mendicant is a beggar, so this is to take up asking for alms

explanation.surface: An unwanted person turns to begging.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being left unclaimed, and literally the act of starting to ask strangers for money.

clue.text: Happy to comply with tradition, primarily for son

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands in for the other

parts.note: to comply is to agree, to consent

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of tradition is taken

explanation.surface: A son is happy to go along with family tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily for son' puts T (the first letter of 'tradition') in place of the S in CONSENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Content means satisfied and at ease, a synonym of happy.

clue.text: The two parts needed to make friend give authorisation

indicators.note: needed to make means the and sits between the pieces that build the friend word

parts.note: a friend is a mate
two parts are this one and that one, so the word joining them is and

explanation.surface: Making a friend takes two halves coming together, and that grants permission.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue's opening as 'M and ATE': the two parts that make up a word for friend, joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mandate is to officially authorise or require something, so it means to give authorisation.

clue.text: Bill wants American university grant

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Bill wants a grant from an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name and 'grant' like funding, but they are a poster and a verb meaning concede.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to concede or acknowledge it, so grant and admit are synonyms.

clue.text: Parking in toll road involved a lot of money

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the parking letter goes within the jumble
involved means tangled, so the letters of toll road are rearranged

parts.note: P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Parking on a toll road costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges TOLL ROAD, and 'in' slips P among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the highest price: paying top dollar means paying a great deal of money.

clue.text: Wren, maybe, or the Arctic cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of the Arctic are scrambled

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers wonder whether they are looking at a wren or an Arctic cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The birds are a decoy: Wren is Sir Christopher Wren, who designed St Paul's Cathedral, and 'cuckoo' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren designed many London churches, so he is an example of a building designer.

clue.text: Prune culinary shrubs and behave playfully

parts.note: to prune a plant is to cut it
capers are the shrubs whose pickled buds are used in cooking

explanation.surface: A gardener trims the herb bushes and frolics about.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for frisking about: to cut capers is to leap and play in a lively, silly way.

clue.text: Passing English pub on green shortly

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter of the colour word is dropped

parts.note: emerald is a shade of green

explanation.surface: Briefly passing an English pub on the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like it means soon, but it trims the D from EMERALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing is fleeting and short-lived, just as ephemeral things last only a short time.

clue.text: Person who's given one parting instructions to cook books

indicators.note: parting means splitting apart, so the letter for one sits in the middle of the cooking word

parts.note: a recipe gives instructions for cooking
the Roman numeral I is one
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone receives a cookery book full of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient is the person who receives something, that is, the one who is given it.

clue.text: Relief after rising in rank makes you beam

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed relief word goes within the rank word

parts.note: to rank is to rate

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: aid is relief, as in disaster relief

explanation.surface: Relief at a promotion makes someone smile broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the relief word to DIA and 'in' places it inside; 'beam' is a smile in the surface but a verb, to shine, in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to send out light, and to radiate is to emit rays, so both mean shine outward.

clue.text: Did long moustache droop to some extent?

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Did someone's moustache sag a little, as if longing for something?
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn for it, so having longed is the same as having yearned.

clue.text: Knot garden creating hazard

indicators.note: a knot is a tangle, so the letters of garden are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An elaborately knotted formal garden poses a risk to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A knot garden is a formal Tudor garden of hedges in intricate patterns; here 'Knot' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a source of risk or peril, a synonym of danger.

clue.text: I start to laugh after autocrat almost gets sack

indicators.note: after means the I and the letter that follows come behind the shortened ruler
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the ruler word is dropped

parts.note: an autocrat is an absolute ruler, a despot

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of laugh

explanation.surface: Someone starts laughing after the near-dictator gets the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like dismissal but here means plunder, as soldiers sack a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a place is to plunder and strip it, which is the meaning of despoil.

clue.text: Clog half of 26s up over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the half is turned round
half of means only the first half of the letters is kept

parts.note: the answer to 26 down is a word for sinks, so its plural is that word with S
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A drain is clogged by half the sinks backing up over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of 26s' takes BAS from BASINS and 'up' turns it into SAB; 'Clog' looks like a verb but is the noun, a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden shoe worn in France and the Low Countries, a type of clog.

clue.text: Individual in Luxor on vacation is reclusive sort

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the one goes between the remaining letters
on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of Luxor are left

parts.note: an individual is one

explanation.surface: A solitary tourist on holiday in Luxor keeps to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like a holiday but empties Luxor of its middle, leaving its two outer letters around the individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner prefers solitude and avoids company, so is a reclusive sort of person.

clue.text: White vestment, uniform given to bishops?

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment worn by clergy
U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet
in chess the bishops are among the pieces, known as men

explanation.surface: A white vestment is a uniform handed out to bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that bishops are chessmen, not clergy, despite the church setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg, so it is a crossword-only sense of white as egg white.

clue.text: North of Indiana boats regularly sink

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of means placed above, so these letters come first
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of boats is taken

parts.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for the state of Indiana

explanation.surface: Boats north of Indiana keep sinking, on the Great Lakes perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a verb about boats but is the noun, a washbasin.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a bowl for washing, and a sink is the same kind of fixture.

clue.text: Vehicle — medic treated ulna in one?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: treated means worked on, so the letters of ulna are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a broken arm bone inside the emergency vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges ULNA to ULAN; with MB that goes 'in' ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is a vehicle that carries the sick and injured to hospital.

clue.text: Endlessly sift loose pieces of rock

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter of the sifting word is dropped

parts.note: to screen is to sift through a mesh

explanation.surface: Someone sifts gravel and stones over and over without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it means ceaselessly but trims the N from SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the mass of small loose stones covering a mountain slope.

clue.text: Boldly go into western part of prison alone

parts.note: to go into a place is to enter it

indicators.note: in an across clue west is the left, so the left-hand half of prison is taken

parts.note: alone means one by one, singly

explanation.surface: A daring inmate walks alone into the west wing of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western part of prison' is PRI, its left-hand half; 'Boldly go' hints at Star Trek, but only 'Boldly' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting enterprisingly means showing initiative and daring, which is acting boldly.
